## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)
- [`sat26-sparse`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-sparse)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Keep one Boolean variable for every declared vertex, including isolated vertices.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $n$ |
| Clauses | $m$ |
| Maximum clause width | $2$ |

## Derivation

1. For each edge uv add $\neg x_u\vee\neg x_v$. Each satisfying assignment is exactly one independent set, and every independent set determines exactly one assignment.

2. The formula has N=n variables and M=m clauses of width at most two. Apply the general-density exact-counting assumption.

3. If m=O(n), the sparse assumption also applies and gives B(n) times a polynomial in the input length. Isolated vertices must remain as free declared variables or contribute the corresponding power of two.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- The qualitative subexponential-in-n counting result is already stated in Corollary 1.3; the displayed quantitative substitution follows Theorem 1.1.
- Counting vertex covers follows by complementing the selected vertex set.

Counting requires a count-preserving encoding and preprocessing, or an explicit correction for multiplicities. The derivation must justify this; decision preservation alone is insufficient.
